function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Practical Tips | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits: 35–55 mph on rural roads, 45–65 mph on highways, 25–35 mph in residential zones.
• “No speed limit” zones exist on some rural roads; drivers must use caution. | • Always obey posted signs; use a GPS that updates speed limits. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | • Check the seat‑belt sign in your vehicle; keep child seats properly installed. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Use a Bluetooth headset or voice‑control. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | • Designate a driver or use rideshare if you’ve had a drink. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Stop signs and traffic signals must be obeyed. | • Always check for pedestrians and cyclists before proceeding. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• The bus must display its stop sign and flashing lights. | • Do not pass a stopped school bus until the lights are off. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals; check mirrors and blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied. | • Keep a safe following distance (at least 2–3 seconds). | | **Headlights** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | • Use low beams in clear weather; high beams only when no other vehicle is present. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | • Pay attention to street signs and meter regulations. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Towing a vehicle requires a proper tow bar and a valid registration. | • Keep registration and insurance documents in the vehicle. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Automated enforcement cameras are used in many cities. | • Adhere to posted speed limits to avoid fines. | | **Special Rules for Motorcycles** | • Helmets are mandatory for riders under 18 and for all riders over 18.
• Must wear protective gear (gloves, jacket, pants). | • Check the motorcycle’s safety equipment before riding. | ### Quick Reference Resources - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official traffic laws, road safety tips, and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text (available online). - **Texas DMV** – Licensing, registration, and driver’s handbook. - **Local County Courts** – For specific traffic violation penalties and court procedures. --- #### How to Stay Informed 1. **Download the TxDOT app** – real‑time traffic alerts and law updates. 2. **Subscribe to the Texas DMV email list** – receive reminders about renewals and new regulations. 3. **Check local news outlets** – they often report on changes to speed limits or new enforcement initiatives. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular traffic situation!
